## Motivation

GLM-5.3 uses DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA). A decode worker needs its index-key pages and scales alongside attention KV to resume generation. The CPU-buffer implementation in the parent PR rejects DSA state. This PR adds that transfer support for GLM-5.3 PD deployments in TDX/Confidential Computing (CC) environments.

This PR is stacked on [#46554](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46554) at `4c1b634eec`, which depends on [#45779](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45779). The GLM-specific diff is relative to that parent.

Tracking issue: #46588

## Modifications

- Pack DSA index-key pages and scales into the CPU transfer buffer and restore them at the destination's physical page indices.
- Skip zero-sized payloads for layers that reuse another layer's top-k indices, while retaining the full component metadata for peer-layout validation.
- Handle empty page-index lists received through the bootstrap protocol.
- Add sparse-page and descriptor-order regressions, real NIXL/UCX transfer coverage, and a GLM-5.3 evaluator using the upstream GSM8K protocol.

This change targets `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`. Compressed DSA tail state and hybrid MLA layouts remain unsupported. The tests below use no MTP, PP/CP or offload.

## Accuracy Tests

Model, fault-injection and performance results below were collected at `753db656a5`. The current revision, `47c4cdf309`, includes upstream changes through `d19f19d68c`; full-model evaluations have not been rerun on this revision.

Tests use `GLM-5.3-W4AFP8` on two TDX hosts with eight H20 GPUs each. Unified uses TP8 on one host; cross-node PD uses TP8 per role, sixteen GPUs in total. Both use W4AFP8 weights, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, page size 64, chunked prefill 2,048, context length 65,536, and DSA backends `flashmla_sparse_q8` for prefill and `flashmla_kv` for decode. CUDA graphs and overlap scheduling are enabled. Radix caching is enabled for unified/prefill and disabled for PD decode.

PD uses a 16 GiB CPU pool per worker, checksum verification, and NIXL/UCX with `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy,self` and `UCX_ACC_DEVICES=''`. PD also sets `SGLANG_MOE_COPY_WEIGHT_VIEWS_BEFORE_H2D=1`, which copies mmap-backed MoE weight slices into separate CPU storage before loading them onto the GPU.

GSM8K follows the [upstream GLM-5.3 GSM8K test](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5828cd49276a419402b316aec0236e5c2161e46d/test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_glm53_eval_mi35x.py): `run_sgl_eval`, all 1,319 questions, zero-shot chat with thinking, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, seed 42, 64 client threads and a 32,768-token output limit. The upstream test sets a 92% threshold for FP8. Both W4AFP8 runs exceed that threshold; the unified run provides a reference using the same checkpoint.

| Test | Unified TP8 | Cross-node PD, TP8 per role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K | 1288/1319 (97.65%) | 1283/1319 (97.27%) |
| Request errors | 0 | 0 |
| Responses at output limit | 1 | 1 |

PD scored five fewer correct answers than unified, a difference of 0.38 percentage points. Responses that reached the output limit are included in both scores.

The upstream logprob parity check passed at 63, 64, 65, 127, 128 and 129 input tokens. It failed at 2,047, 2,048, 2,049, 4,097 and 8,193 tokens, including on repeated requests to the same unified server. Strict parity remains unresolved for these inputs; passing GSM8K and transfer checksums does not establish logprob parity.

Generation checks returned the expected answer for short prompts and prompts longer than `index_topk=2048`. A repeated 4,431-token prompt reused 4,416 cached tokens and returned the expected answer.

At `47c4cdf309`, all 148 regression tests passed, covering buffer lifecycle, queue cleanup, checksum and real NIXL/UCX CUDA transfers. Pre-commit passed.

```bash
python test/manual/disaggregation/eval_glm53_cpu_buffer_pd.py \
  --url "$ENDPOINT_URL" --model glm-5.3 --output-dir "$RESULT_DIR"
```

Cross-node fault tests inject failures during decode receive-buffer allocation, prefill send-buffer allocation, and after a real NIXL write submission. Requests go directly to both workers, bypassing router retries.

Each injected request returned HTTP 500 from both peers. Four subsequent requests returned correct answers without restarting either worker. All sixteen rank pools returned to zero allocated bytes and pending handles, and both request queues emptied. In the post-submission case, buffers were retained until outstanding transfers completed. Host crashes and network partitions were not tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Serving sanity checks use upstream `sglang.bench_serving`: `random-ids`, nominal 1,024-token inputs, 128 output tokens, range ratio 1, seed 42 and unlimited request rate. Each configuration was run once, serially, with 16 warmup requests followed by 80 measured requests. `--flush-cache` clears both PD workers after warmup. The default text sampling mode can change input lengths during server-side retokenization.

| Deployment | H20 GPUs | Concurrency | Output tokens/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unified TP8 | 8 | 1 | 62.63 | 282.74 | 13.88 |
| Unified TP8 | 8 | 16 | 270.68 | 3062.77 | 35.00 |
| Cross-node PD, TP8 per role | 16 | 1 | 58.11 | 437.11 | 13.91 |
| Cross-node PD, TP8 per role | 16 | 16 | 332.11 | 1237.72 | 34.71 |

All 320 measured requests completed with 128 output tokens each. CUDA graphs and overlap scheduling remain enabled, with a running-request limit of 32. MTP, checksum verification and fault injection are disabled for timing. PD requests use the mini_lb router to coordinate prefill and decode. The hosts were shared, and no repeated measurements were collected. PD uses twice as many GPUs as unified.

```bash
python -m sglang.bench_serving \
  --backend sglang --base-url "$ENDPOINT_URL" --model /models/GLM-5.3-W4AFP8 \
  --served-model-name glm-5.3 \
  --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \
  --random-range-ratio 1 --seed 42 --num-prompts 80 --warmup-requests 16 \
  --flush-cache --max-concurrency "$CONCURRENCY" --output-file "$RESULT_FILE"
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the repository's pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit and real-transfer tests.
- [x] Update deployment documentation.
- [x] Run paired unified/cross-node PD GSM8K evaluation.
- [x] Report deployment settings and parity limitations.
- [x] Complete and review cross-node fault recovery tests.
- [x] Complete and review serving performance sanity checks.

 Currently, we support Mooncake and NIXL as the transfer engine.
 
+## NIXL CPU buffers for TDX/CC deployments
+
+On NVIDIA CUDA deployments where NIXL cannot access GPU memory directly, you can
+stage KV transfers through pageable CPU memory. Enable these options on **both
+prefill and decode**, in addition to `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`:
+
+```bash
+--nixl-use-cpu-buffer --nixl-cpu-buffer-size-gb 16
+```
+
+Each worker allocates its own bounded host pool (16 GiB by default). Prefill
+copies each KV chunk from GPU to CPU, NIXL writes it to the decode worker's host
+pool, and decode copies the assembled request to its GPU KV cache before
+reporting transfer success. NIXL registers the host pool instead of the GPU KV
+buffers. Host allocations are pageable, including when CUDA pinned allocations
+are unavailable in confidential computing (CC) mode.
+
+This option changes the memory path only. It does not enable TDX, GPU CC,
+attestation, or transport encryption. Configure those separately for your
+security requirements. Choose a NIXL backend and transport that support host
+memory in your deployment. For UCX on a TDX/CC guest that rejects CUDA host
+registration, set the following environment variables before starting **both**
+workers:
+
+```bash
+export UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy,self
+export UCX_ACC_DEVICES=''
+```
+
+NIXL versions that check for CUDA support require `cuda_copy` in `UCX_TLS` when
+GPUs are visible. Setting `UCX_ACC_DEVICES` to an empty string disables UCX's
+accelerator memory domains, preventing host registration from calling
+`cuMemHostRegister`. SGLang still performs GPU/CPU copies through PyTorch. Use
+this profile only with CPU-buffer transfers; it does not provide direct GPU
+transfers through UCX.
+
+Use the same SGLang revision, model, KV layout, page size, and attention TP size
+on both sides. This initial path supports contiguous MHA and MLA KV buffers with
+PP, CP, and DCP sizes of one. Hybrid GDN models such as Qwen3.5 and
+Qwen3.8-Flash-Next are supported.
+The final prefill chunk sends the conv and recurrent state, including
+request-scoped PLE state, through the same host pool. For Qwen3.8-Flash-Next,
+it also sends the QSA pending key and RoPE rings and the compressed index-key
+pages for the full prompt. Decode restores both KV and state before allowing
+generation. Both sides must have identical state layouts and attention TP sizes.
+With `--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum`, verification includes all three state
+components using their respective physical indices.
+
+For DSA models such as GLM-5.3, the final chunk also transfers index-key pages
+and their scales. Layers that reuse another layer's top-k have no index-key
+payload. Decode restores these pages before generation; KV checksum verification
+covers the index-key cache as well. Use matching page sizes and skip-topk layouts
+on both workers. Compressed DSA tail state is not supported.
+
+It does not support speculative decoding, hybrid MLA layouts, other extra state
+components beyond Mamba/GDN, QSA and DSA, PLE embedding offload, HiCache,
+HiSparse, decode KV offload, decode host receive, GPU staging, or runtime PD role switching.
+Do not combine `--nixl-use-cpu-buffer` with `--enable-kv-cache-sharding`.
+Sharding produces noncontiguous send positions, while CPU-buffer transfers
+require contiguous send slices. The server rejects this combination at startup.
+For Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, PLE embedding offload defaults to disabled in this
+mode; explicitly enabling it is rejected. Keep the embedding table on the
+GPU and budget GPU memory accordingly. With the official FP8 checkpoint, pair
+TP2 with EP2 (`--tp-size 2 --ep-size 2`) to keep expert projections aligned with
+the checkpoint's quantization blocks.
+Unsupported local configurations and peer layouts fail explicitly.
+
+On decode, this mode defaults `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup` to
+`cpu_tensor`, which uses per-request CPU tensors and preserves QSA pending
+and compressed state when a decode request is retracted. An explicit `none`
+value is preserved. The `host_pool` backend is rejected because it allocates a
+CUDA-registered HiCache pool even when incoming KV uses CPU buffers.
+
+Size the pool for concurrent requests: decode holds every received KV page for
+a request, together with its Mamba/GDN, QSA or DSA state when present, until GPU
+restoration completes. Prefill holds each packed chunk until its NIXL transfer
+settles. Pool exhaustion fails the affected
+request instead of waiting for pool space. An aborted decode request
+keeps its host region, GPU KV slots, and auxiliary slot until all TP ranks
+confirm that the required prefill abort acknowledgments have arrived. A timeout
+alone never makes these resources reusable. If a peer is lost, its resources
+can remain reserved until the worker restarts.
+
+CPU copies add latency and host-memory traffic. Measure end-to-end latency,
+throughput, and host-memory use for your workload before enabling this path in
+production.
+
 ## Decode allocation policy
 
 By default, decode reserves each request's destination KV slots before prefill

+# Cross-node CPU-buffer fault injection
+
+Use isolated prefill/decode test servers with the same model and TP layout.
+This helper instruments the Python CPU-buffer allocator and NIXL submission
+boundary; it does not modify production source or inject network packet loss.
+
+On both hosts, prepend this directory to `PYTHONPATH` before launching the
+server and choose a writable directory for the worker event logs:
+
+```bash
+export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/test/manual/disaggregation/cpu_buffer_fault_injection:$PWD/python:$PWD"
+export SGLANG_CPU_FAULT_DIR=/tmp/sglang-cpu-buffer-fault
+mkdir -p "$SGLANG_CPU_FAULT_DIR"
+rm -f "$SGLANG_CPU_FAULT_DIR/arm"
+```
+
+Launch the servers with `--nixl-use-cpu-buffer` and checksum verification.
+After readiness, run the following cases separately:
+
+| Host to arm | File content | Injected failure |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Decode | `allocate` | Receive-buffer allocation raises `BufferError` |
+| Prefill | `allocate` | Send-buffer allocation raises `BufferError` |
+| Prefill | `post` | `transfer()` submits a real NIXL write, then raises |
+
+For example, on the selected host:
+
+```bash
+printf '%s' allocate > "$SGLANG_CPU_FAULT_DIR/arm"
+```
+
+Submit the same request directly to both `/generate` endpoints, with a shared
+`rid`, `bootstrap_host`, `bootstrap_port`, and unique `bootstrap_room`. Bypassing
+the router keeps retries from hiding the injected request failure. Check that
+the decode response reports an abort/error and that the worker JSONL logs record
+an `injected` event. Remove `arm` before issuing recovery requests:
+
+```bash
+rm "$SGLANG_CPU_FAULT_DIR/arm"
+```
+
+Run four more paired requests with fresh request and room IDs. Require all four
+to succeed, no checksum mismatch, empty disaggregation queues, and zero pool
+`allocations`, `bytes`, and `pending` counts on every rank after cleanup. For
+`post`, the `send_exception` event must show retained allocations and pending
+handles before cleanup. This checks ownership after a posted write, rather than
+only failure before submission.
+
+Each process injects each fault kind once per lifetime. Restart the isolated
+servers to repeat a kind. A subsequent server launch without this directory on
+`PYTHONPATH` and without `SGLANG_CPU_FAULT_DIR` runs without instrumentation.

+"""Opt-in fault injection for externally launched CPU-buffer PD workers.
+
+Prepend this directory to PYTHONPATH and set SGLANG_CPU_FAULT_DIR to a directory
+shared by the worker processes on each host. Write ``allocate`` or ``post`` into its ``arm``
+file to fail one matching operation per worker process per fault kind. Remove
+``arm`` before recovery requests. Inspect the per-process JSONL event logs.
+Only use on isolated test servers. No fault is injected without an arm file.
+"""
+
+import importlib.abc
+import importlib.machinery
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import threading
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = os.environ.get("SGLANG_CPU_FAULT_DIR")
+
+
+def install(module):
+    root = Path(ROOT)
+    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    seen = set()
+
+    def event(event_name, **fields):
+        with (root / f"{os.getpid()}.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
+            stream.write(
+                json.dumps({"time": time.time(), "event": event_name, **fields}) + "\n"
+            )
+
+    def armed(kind):
+        try:
+            value = (root / "arm").read_text().strip()
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            return False
+        if value != kind or kind in seen:
+            return False
+        seen.add(kind)
+        event("injected", kind=kind)
+        return True
+
+    pool = module.CpuBufferPool
+    allocate = pool.allocate
+
+    def fault_allocate(self, size):
+        if armed("allocate"):
+            raise BufferError("Injected CPU buffer pool exhaustion")
+        return allocate(self, size)
+
+    pool.allocate = fault_allocate
+    mixin = module.CpuBufferMixin
+    send = mixin._send_cpu_chunk
+
+    class AgentProxy:
+        def __init__(self, agent):
+            self.agent = agent
+
+        def __getattr__(self, name):
+            return getattr(self.agent, name)
+
+        def transfer(self, handle):
+            result = self.agent.transfer(handle)
+            if armed("post"):
+                # The write really was posted. The caller must drain its handle
+                # before reusing the source or acknowledging the peer's abort.
+                raise RuntimeError("Injected failure after NIXL write submission")
+            return result
+
+    def fault_send(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        if not isinstance(self.agent, AgentProxy):
+            self.agent = AgentProxy(self.agent)
+        try:
+            return send(self, *args, **kwargs)
+        except Exception:
+            with self._cpu_pool._lock:
+                event(
+                    "send_exception",
+                    allocations=len(self._cpu_pool._ranges),
+                    pending=len(self._cpu_pool._pending),
+                )
+            raise
+
+    mixin._send_cpu_chunk = fault_send
+    init = pool.__init__
+
+    def monitored_init(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        init(self, *args, **kwargs)
+
+        def monitor():
+            while True:
+                with self._lock:
+                    fields = dict(
+                        allocations=len(self._ranges),
+                        bytes=sum(self._ranges.values()),
+                        pending=len(self._pending),
+                    )
+                event("pool", **fields)
+                time.sleep(1)
+
+        threading.Thread(target=monitor, daemon=True).start()
+
+    pool.__init__ = monitored_init
+    event("installed")
+
+
+class FaultFinder(importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder):
+    def find_spec(self, fullname, path, target=None):
+        if fullname != "sglang.srt.disaggregation.nixl.cpu_buffer":
+            return None
+        spec = importlib.machinery.PathFinder.find_spec(fullname, path)
+        original = spec.loader.exec_module
+
+        def execute(module):
+            original(module)
+            install(module)
+
+        spec.loader.exec_module = execute
+        return spec
+
+
+if ROOT:
+    sys.meta_path.insert(0, FaultFinder())

+"""Validate externally launched unified/PD endpoints with upstream test helpers.
+
+Run ``parity-reference`` against a fresh unified server, then ``parity`` against
+its matching PD router. Both must use identical TP/backend/page/chunk settings.
+Run ``gsm8k`` against each endpoint with the same evaluator arguments. Server
+lifecycle and cross-node placement are external so this works with SSH hosts.
+The parity tolerance is fixed before either run; failures never widen it.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import time
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import requests
+from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+from sglang.test.kits.pd_parity_kit import PDLogprobParityMixin
+from sglang.test.run_eval import run_eval_once
+from sglang.test.simple_eval_mixed_prefix_gsm8k import GSM8KEval
+
+
+class EndpointParity(PDLogprobParityMixin, unittest.TestCase):
+    parity_max_new_tokens = 8
+    parity_logprob_delta = 1e-3
+
+
+def boundary_prompts(model, page_size, chunk_size):
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, trust_remote_code=True)
+    filler = tokenizer.encode(
+        "Archive note: the weather was mild, the office lights were on, "
+        "and no unusual event was reported. ",
+        add_special_tokens=False,
+    )
+    question = tokenizer.encode("\nSummarize the archive:", add_special_tokens=False)
+    lengths = sorted(
+        {n + d for n in (page_size, chunk_size, 2 * chunk_size) for d in (-1, 0, 1)}
+        | {4 * chunk_size + 1, 8 * chunk_size + 1}
+    )
+    if lengths[0] < len(question):
+        raise ValueError("Page boundary is too short for the parity question")
+    body = filler * (max(lengths) // len(filler) + 1)
+    return [body[: n - len(question)] + question for n in lengths]
+
+
+def health(url):
+    response = requests.get(url.rstrip("/") + "/health", timeout=30)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+
+
+def compare(case, reference, actual, label):
+    errors = []
+    try:
+        case._assert_logprob_parity(reference=reference, actual=actual, label=label)
+    except AssertionError as exc:
+        errors.append(str(exc))
+    expected = reference["output_token_logprobs"]
+    observed = actual["output_token_logprobs"]
+    matching_ids = [x[1] for x in expected] == [x[1] for x in observed]
+    # Logprobs after different token histories are not comparable.
+    delta = (
+        max(abs(a[0] - b[0]) for a, b in zip(expected, observed))
+        if matching_ids and expected
+        else None
+    )
+    return {
+        "token_ids_equal": matching_ids,
+        "max_logprob_delta": delta,
+        "errors": errors,
+    }
+
+
+def run_parity(args):
+    case = EndpointParity()
+    report = {
+        "mode": args.mode,
+        "model": args.model,
+        "tp": args.tp,
+        "page_size": args.page_size,
+        "chunk_size": args.chunk_size,
+        "max_new_tokens": case.parity_max_new_tokens,
+        "logprob_delta": case.parity_logprob_delta,
+        "cases": [],
+    }
+    if args.mode == "parity-reference":
+        prompts = boundary_prompts(args.model, args.page_size, args.chunk_size)
+        references = None
+        flush_urls = [args.url]
+    else:
+        if not args.reference or not args.prefill_url or not args.decode_url:
+            raise ValueError("parity requires reference, prefill-url and decode-url")
+        ref = json.loads(Path(args.reference).read_text())
+        for key in (
+            "model",
+            "tp",
+            "page_size",
+            "chunk_size",
+            "max_new_tokens",
+            "logprob_delta",
+        ):
+            if ref[key] != report[key]:
+                raise ValueError(f"Reference configuration mismatch: {key}")
+        if not ref.get("passed"):
+            raise ValueError("Unified repeatability check did not pass")
+        references = ref["cases"]
+        prompts = [row["input_ids"] for row in references]
+        flush_urls = [args.prefill_url, args.decode_url]
+    health(args.url)
+    for i, prompt in enumerate(prompts):
+        for url in flush_urls:
+            case._flush_cache(url)
+        actual = case._generate(base_url=args.url, input_ids=prompt)
+        if references is None:
+            case._flush_cache(args.url)
+            reference = case._generate(base_url=args.url, input_ids=prompt)
+        else:
+            reference = references[i]["actual"]
+        row = {
+            "input_ids": prompt,
+            "actual": actual,
+            "reference": reference,
+            **compare(case, reference, actual, f"prompt_tokens={len(prompt)}"),
+        }
+        report["cases"].append(row)
+        print(
+            json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "prompt_tokens": len(prompt),
+                    **{
+                        k: row[k]
+                        for k in ("token_ids_equal", "max_logprob_delta", "errors")
+                    },
+                }
+            ),
+            flush=True,
+        )
+        Path(args.output).write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
+    health(args.url)
+    for url in flush_urls:
+        health(url)
+    report["passed"] = all(not row["errors"] for row in report["cases"])
+    Path(args.output).write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
+    if not report["passed"]:
+        raise AssertionError("Parity failed; see the complete per-prompt report")
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("mode", choices=("parity-reference", "parity", "gsm8k"))
+    parser.add_argument("--url", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--tp", type=int, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--reference")
+    parser.add_argument("--prefill-url")
+    parser.add_argument("--decode-url")
+    parser.add_argument("--page-size", type=int, default=16)
+    parser.add_argument("--chunk-size", type=int, default=128)
+    parser.add_argument("--num-examples", type=int, default=512)
+    parser.add_argument("--num-threads", type=int, default=16)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=512)
+    parser.add_argument("--gsm8k-data-path")
+    parser.add_argument("--accuracy-threshold", type=float, default=0.83)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-accuracy-drop", type=float, default=0.05)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    Path(args.output).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    if args.mode != "gsm8k":
+        run_parity(args)
+        return
+    health(args.url)
+    # Match the Qwen3.5-35B PP test's five-shot completion protocol. The
+    # evaluator excludes the five demonstration questions from the scored set.
+    os.environ.setdefault("OPENAI_API_KEY", "EMPTY")
+    config = SimpleNamespace(
+        model=args.model,
+        api="completion",
+        max_tokens=args.max_tokens,
+        num_examples=args.num_examples,
+        num_threads=args.num_threads,
+        num_shots=5,
+        temperature=0.0,
+        top_p=1.0,
+    )
+    evaluator = GSM8KEval(
+        num_examples=config.num_examples,
+        num_threads=config.num_threads,
+        num_shots=config.num_shots,
+        data_path=args.gsm8k_data_path,
+    )
+    start = time.time()
+    result, latency, sampler = run_eval_once(
+        config, args.url.rstrip("/") + "/v1", evaluator
+    )
+    health(args.url)
+    errors = []
+    if len(result.convos) != args.num_examples:
+        errors.append("Evaluator did not score the requested number of examples")
+    if len(sampler._completion_tokens) != args.num_examples:
+        errors.append("Missing successful completion responses or usage records")
+    if any(not convo[-1]["content"].strip() for convo in result.convos):
+        errors.append("Empty completion response")
+    if result.score < args.accuracy_threshold:
+        errors.append(f"Accuracy {result.score} < {args.accuracy_threshold}")
+    baseline_score = None
+    if args.reference:
+        reference = json.loads(Path(args.reference).read_text())
+        if not reference.get("passed"):
+            errors.append("Unified reference did not pass")
+        if reference["config"] != vars(config) or reference["tp"] != args.tp:
+            errors.append("Unified reference configuration mismatch")
+        baseline_score = reference["score"]
+        if result.score < baseline_score - args.max_accuracy_drop:
+            errors.append("PD accuracy drop exceeds the configured tolerance")
+        if [c[0] for c in reference["convos"]] != [c[0] for c in result.convos]:
+            errors.append("Unified and PD evaluated different prompts")
+    report = {
+        "mode": args.mode,
+        "tp": args.tp,
+        "config": vars(config),
+        "score": result.score,
+        "metrics": result.metrics,
+        "accuracy_threshold": args.accuracy_threshold,
+        "max_accuracy_drop": args.max_accuracy_drop,
+        "baseline_score": baseline_score,
+        "convos": result.convos,
+        "completion_tokens": sampler._completion_tokens,
+        "responses_at_token_limit": sum(
+            n == args.max_tokens for n in sampler._completion_tokens
+        ),
+        "elapsed_s": time.time() - start,
+        "evaluator_latency_s": latency,
+        "errors": errors,
+        "passed": not errors,
+    }
+    Path(args.output).write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                k: v
+                for k, v in report.items()
+                if k not in ("convos", "completion_tokens")
+            }
+        ),
+        flush=True,
+    )
+    if errors:
+        raise AssertionError("GSM8K acceptance failed; see the saved report")
+    print("EVALUATION_COMPLETE", args.output, flush=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+            spec.loader.exec_module(self.hook)
+        self.hook.ROOT = str(self.root)
+
+        class Pool:
+            def __init__(self):
+                self._lock = threading.Lock()
+                self._ranges = {}
+                self._pending = []
+
+            def allocate(self, size):
+                return size
+
+        class Mixin:
+            def _send_cpu_chunk(self):
+                self._cpu_pool._ranges[0] = 256
+                self._cpu_pool._pending.append("handle")
+                return self.agent.transfer("handle")
+
+        self.module = SimpleNamespace(CpuBufferPool=Pool, CpuBufferMixin=Mixin)
+        self.hook.install(self.module)
+        with patch.object(threading.Thread, "start"):
+            self.pool = Pool()
+
+    def events(self):
+        return [
+            json.loads(line)
+            for line in (self.root / f"{os.getpid()}.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()
+        ]
+
+    def test_unarmed_allocator_is_unchanged(self):
+        self.assertEqual(self.pool.allocate(256), 256)
+        self.assertFalse(any(row["event"] == "injected" for row in self.events()))
+
+    def test_allocation_fault_is_buffer_error_and_fires_once(self):
+        (self.root / "arm").write_text("allocate")
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(BufferError, "Injected"):
+            self.pool.allocate(256)
+        self.assertEqual(self.pool.allocate(256), 256)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [row["kind"] for row in self.events() if row["event"] == "injected"],
+            ["allocate"],
+        )
+
+    def test_post_fault_occurs_after_transfer_and_retains_ownership(self):
+        (self.root / "arm").write_text("post")
+        submitted = []
+        manager = self.module.CpuBufferMixin()
+        manager._cpu_pool = self.pool
+        manager.agent = SimpleNamespace(
+            transfer=lambda handle: submitted.append(handle)
+        )

+            manager._send_cpu_chunk()
+        self.assertEqual(submitted, ["handle"])
+        events = self.events()
+        self.assertEqual(
